SpecDocument.mission: Establish the Docking Protocol as the non-negotiable Central Nervous System (CNS) for all future Claude ↔ implementation-engine communication. This foundation must be production-grade, strictly validated, fully auditable, and must include a persistent Failure Memory system so the CNS can learn from every blocked or failed specification. The goal is to create an infrastructure that prevents repeated mistakes and becomes measurably stronger over time under Path A (surgical evolution).
SpecDocument.scope: Create the complete docking/ directory structure including memory/. Implement strict Pydantic-based contracts (SpecDocument, ChangeTrace, FailureRecord). Implement a non-bypassable pre_implementation_validation() gate with structured audit logging. Implement a persistent Failure Memory system that records every validation failure and makes it queryable. Create a read-only status + audit + memory surface. Integrate docking health + recent failures into main.py boot sequence.
SpecDocument.non_goals: Do not implement full lifecycle state machine, dependency graph, or ImplementationReport writer yet. Do not perform large-scale restructuring or renaming of the existing project. Do not implement any cognitive, action, or evolution modules.

target.allowed_files: docking/** core/contracts/docking/** core/contracts/spec_protocol.py tests/test_docking_protocol.py main.py core/paths.py

definition.implementation_requirements:
Create docking/ with specs/, reports/, contracts/, registry/, protocol/, audit/, and memory/ subdirectories.
Implement SpecDocument, ChangeTrace, and FailureRecord as strict Pydantic v2 BaseModel classes with full field validation and no extra fields allowed.
Implement validate_spec_before_implementation() as the single non-bypassable gate. Every call must: - Perform mechanical validation of the spec - Query recent failures from docking/memory/failure_log.jsonl - Include relevant_past_failures in the validation result - Append a structured JSONL entry to docking/audit/validation_audit.jsonl
Implement Failure Memory system in docking/memory/failure_memory.py with at minimum: - log_spec_failure(spec_id, failure_category, reason, issues, timestamp) - get_recent_failures(limit=20) - get_failures_by_category(category) - FailureRecord Pydantic model (spec_id, failure_category, reason, issues, timestamp, validator_version)
Create docking/specification_protocol.py exposing: - docking_protocol_status() - get_recent_validation_audit(limit=10) - get_recent_failures(limit=10)
Update main.py boot_checks() to call docking_protocol_status() and include both docking health and number of recent failures in the boot report.
All code must use type hints, comprehensive docstrings, proper exception handling (no bare excepts), and deterministic behavior.

criterion.description: docking/specs/, docking/reports/, docking/contracts/, docking/registry/, docking/protocol/, docking/audit/, and docking/memory/ directories exist with correct internal structure.
criterion.verification: Use pathlib to assert all seven directories exist under docking/. Confirm docking/memory/ contains failure_log.jsonl placeholder or is ready for JSONL appends.

criterion.description: SpecDocument.py, ChangeTrace.py, and FailureRecord.py exist, are importable, and define strict Pydantic v2 models. Instantiation with invalid data must raise ValidationError.
criterion.verification: Run python import test + try/except ValidationError test on all three models. All must pass strict validation.

criterion.description: pre_implementation_validation() exists, correctly accepts valid specs and rejects malformed ones, always writes to audit log, and includes relevant_past_failures in its result when past failures exist for similar issues.
criterion.verification: Call validator with valid SPEC-0001 → status="passed" + audit entry written. Call validator with malformed spec → status="blocked" + FailureRecord written to failure_log.jsonl + relevant_past_failures shown in result. Inspect last lines of both audit and failure_log to confirm required fields.

criterion.description: Failure Memory system is functional. log_spec_failure() and get_recent_failures() work correctly. Failures are persisted as structured JSONL.
criterion.verification: Manually log two different failure categories. Call get_recent_failures(5) and get_failures_by_category("bad_acceptance_criteria"). Both must return the correct records with all fields populated.

criterion.description: main.py boot_checks() successfully calls docking protocol status functions and reports both docking health and recent failure count without exceptions.
criterion.verification: Execute boot sequence. Confirm output contains docking health status and something like "Recent Failures: X" or equivalent. No ImportError or AttributeError related to docking or memory.

definition.rollback_expectations: If this spec is rejected or superseded, the entire docking/ folder (including memory/ and all audit + failure logs) must remain intact. No automatic deletion of CNS infrastructure is permitted.

impact.deploy: Adds mandatory docking CNS health + recent failure count to every boot. Future deploy_check.py runs must validate that the docking layer is present, passes validation, has audit logging active, and has a working failure memory system.
impact.risks: Medium if future specs ignore the docking gate or fail to query past failures. Mitigation: Missing audit entries or failure to reference relevant past failures will now be detectable in ImplementationReports and boot checks.
